training-sat.title: SAT analysis workbench
training-sat.purpose: Job and task analysis: task inventories, DIF ratings, train / no-train decisions and the task-to-training matrix.

training-sat-role.title: Job analysis
training-sat-role.purpose: The task inventory of a role, its DIF survey, training decisions and coverage by learning objectives.

training-sat-task.title: Task analysis
training-sat-task.purpose: DIF ratings, the training decision, linked objectives and the impact of a change to one task.

training-sat-changes.title: SAT changes
training-sat-changes.purpose: Task changes and the review items they opened for courses and qualification standards.

training-sat-report.title: Traceability report
training-sat-report.purpose: Export the task-to-training traceability of a role in English or Arabic.

training-sat-survey.title: DIF survey
training-sat-survey.purpose: Rate the tasks of your role on difficulty, importance and frequency when the survey is open.

training-accreditation.title: Accreditation readiness
training-accreditation.purpose: Self-evaluate training programmes against generic SAT criteria, with evidence from Kafa'a and gap owners.

training-accreditation-selfeval.title: Self-evaluation
training-accreditation-selfeval.purpose: Rate each criterion, attach suggested evidence, own the gaps and finalise with a second person.

training-accreditation-report.title: Self-evaluation report
training-accreditation-report.purpose: Generate the self-evaluation report in English or Arabic (demo, not an accreditation decision).

training-sat-future.title: Task layer: AI exposure and change horizon
training-sat-future.purpose: Every SAT task rated on the OECD AI capability dimensions: what the tool will do, what people will still own, by when, and the skills it needs.

decision.overrideHint: The training manager decided differently from the DIF rule, with a reason

restricted.body: Security, safeguards and cyber tasks are analysed and trained outside Kafa'a. Kafa'a shows them as restricted placeholders only: no title, rating, link or change.

dif.title: DIF survey
dif.scaleNote: Consensus per dimension is the mean rounded half up; ratings spread by 3 or more are flagged as a disagreement.

rule.title: The DIF decision rule
rule.overtrain: Importance 4+, difficulty 3+ and frequency 2 or less: overtrain (train beyond mastery and refresh)
rule.rare_moderate: Otherwise difficulty 3 and frequency 2 or less: train
rule.low: Otherwise: no train (learned on the job)
rule.source: Generic SAT practice (IAEA TRS-380 / NG-T-2.8). The training manager can decide differently, with a reason that is audited and ledgered.

reasons.dif_overtrain: Important ({i}), difficult ({d}) and rarely performed ({f}): overtrain
reasons.dif_refresh: Plan periodic refresher training (continuing training or a JPM)
reasons.dif_important: Importance {i} of 5 needs formal training (D {d}, F {f})
reasons.dif_difficult: Difficulty {d} of 5 is too high to learn on the job (I {i}, F {f})
reasons.dif_rare_moderate: Moderately difficult ({d}) and rarely practised ({f}): train (I {i})
reasons.dif_low: Low importance ({i}), easy ({d}) or frequent ({f}): learned on the job
reasons.dif_insufficient: {n} of {min} SME ratings so far: no proposal yet
reasons.dif_disagreement: Raters disagree (spread D {d}, I {i}, F {f}): discuss before deciding
reasons.dif_override: The training manager decided "{decision}" instead, with a reason
reasons.accr_gaps: {n} criteria rated 1 or 2 are gaps with owners
reasons.accr_unrated: {n} criteria not yet rated count as 0
reasons.fx_human_core: Human core: AI reaches the need on {k} of {n} rated dimensions, fewer than half
reasons.fx_critical_keep: AI reaches the need on all {n} dimensions, but this is a critical task: a qualified person stays accountable and the tool assists
reasons.fx_all_covered: AI reaches the need on all {n} rated dimensions: parts of the task can be automated, a person verifies the result
reasons.fx_some_covered: AI reaches the need on {k} of {n} rated dimensions: the tool assists, a person owns the outcome
reasons.fx_dim_covered: {dim}: the task needs level {need}; AI capability is level {ai} (covered)
reasons.fx_dim_gap: {dim}: the task needs level {need}; AI capability is level {ai} (people own this)
reasons.fx_horizon: Compared at the change horizon: {horizon} (planning assumption)

sat.intro: Job and task analysis behind every qualification card and course: who does what, how difficult, important and frequent it is, whether it is trained, and which objective, course, module or JPM covers it.
sat.analysesBody: One analysis per role. Coverage is the share of train-selected tasks with at least one learning objective.

survey.calloutBody: {n} tasks of your role are waiting for your ratings.
survey.intro: As a subject-matter expert in your role, rate each task on difficulty, importance and frequency. Training staff combine the ratings into a train / no-train decision.
survey.noneTitle: No DIF survey for you right now
survey.noneBody: Surveys open for subject-matter experts (a Kafa'a SME profile) when training staff analyse their role. You will get a notification.
survey.anonymity: Training staff see who rated; the decision uses the consensus of all raters.
survey.scales: Difficulty: how hard to perform correctly. Importance: consequence of doing it wrong. Frequency: how often you perform it (1 = less than yearly, 5 = weekly or more).

role.intro: Task inventory, DIF survey and training decisions for this role, and how each training task is covered by objectives and training.

moveBody.survey: Subject-matter experts who hold this role (Kafa'a SME profile) are notified and can rate its tasks.
moveBody.approved: Every active task has a training decision. Approving freezes this version of the job analysis; later task changes go through SAT changes. Recorded in the evidence ledger.
moveBody.draft: The analysis returns to draft so tasks can be added or re-rated. Reopening an approved analysis starts a new version.

role.addTaskBody: Add a task found in the job analysis. Tasks linked to training change only through a SAT change.
role.inventoryHint: Open a task to rate it, decide or link it to training.
role.noTasks: No tasks in this analysis yet

decide.title: Training decision

means.train: formal initial training to the task standard
means.overtrain: train beyond initial mastery and refresh periodically
means.no_train: no formal training; learned and checked on the job

decide.insufficient: {n} of {min} ratings: a decision needs at least {min} SME ratings.
decide.tmOnly: Only the training manager records train, no-train or overtrain.
decide.confirmBody: The decision follows the DIF rule. It is audited and recorded in the evidence ledger.
decide.overrideBody: The DIF rule proposes "{rule}". Give the reason for deciding differently; it is audited and recorded in the evidence ledger.

links.title: Learning objectives and training
links.eyebrow: Task → objective → course, module or JPM
links.unlinkBody: Remove the link to {code}? If this is the last objective of a training task, it becomes a coverage gap.
links.gapBody: This task is selected for training but no learning objective covers it. Link one or write one.
links.linkBody: Objectives of this role's curriculum courses and SAT objectives written for the role.
links.writeBody: Write the objective with its conditions and standard, in both languages. It is linked to this task when saved.
links.textHint: For example: "Given the approved procedure, align the valve line-up with independent verification, without error on critical steps."

matrix.explain: A coverage gap is a task selected for training (train or overtrain) with no learning objective. An overtrain task also needs a refresher: a continuing-training course or a JPM.
matrix.orphansBody: Objectives of this role's curriculum that no task links to: remove them or link them to the task they serve.

impact.title: Change impact
impact.eyebrow: What a change to this task touches
impact.openTitle: A change is open for this task
impact.itemsNote: Metadata only: id, topic and difficulty. Item text and keys never leave the secure bank.
impact.confirmTitle: Record the change and open review items
impact.confirmBody: This opens one review item for each of the {c} courses and {s} qualification standards linked to the task. Recorded in the evidence ledger.

changes.intro: Every task change lists what it touched and opens one review item per course and qualification standard. Standards are revised with the existing qualification-standard revision.
changes.noneBody: Record a change from a task page when a task, procedure or standard changes.
changes.impactLine: Impact: {c} courses, {s} standards, {j} JPMs, {i} assessment items (metadata only)
changes.noItems: No linked course or standard: nothing to review.
changes.noChangeReason: Why no change is needed (at least 5 characters)
changes.reviseReason: Change reason for the new version

confirmBody.updated: "{item}" has been updated for this change.
confirmBody.revised: "{item}" was revised to a new version; the item closes with a link to it.
confirmBody.no_change: "{item}" needs no change. The reason is kept with the item.
confirmBody.revise_std: Creates a new version of "{item}" and flags every current record for review (existing qualification-standard revision; ledgered). Then close the item as revised.

changes.note: Closing the last item closes the change; opening and closing a change are recorded in the evidence ledger.

redesign.title: Courses flagged for redesign
redesign.body: Flagged by the training-effectiveness review. Open the tasks each course trains to record a SAT change with the trigger "effectiveness review".
redesign.noTasks: No analysed task links to this course (restricted or not yet analysed)

report.traceIntro: The task-to-training traceability of a role, ready to print, save as PDF or download.
report.serIntro: The self-evaluation report, ready to print, save as PDF or download, in English or Arabic.
report.traceFooter: Kafa'a concept demo with synthetic data. Security, safeguards and cyber tasks are restricted and managed outside Kafa'a.
report.methodBody: Generic, paraphrased criteria based on the public IAEA description of the systematic approach to training and FANR-REG-16 Art. 9. They are not the text of any accreditation body. Ratings: 1 not met, 2 partly met, 3 largely met, 4 met; readiness counts unrated criteria as 0.
report.serFooter: A readiness self-check generated by the Kafa'a concept with synthetic data. Kafa'a is not an authority: no accreditation, certification or regulatory status follows from this report.

accr.intro: Self-evaluate each training programme against generic SAT-based criteria, with evidence Kafa'a already holds, owners for every gap and a second person to finalise.
accr.demoBody: Kafa'a helps prepare evidence for external evaluations. It mirrors and never decides: no accreditation status follows from a readiness score.
accr.tileGapsSub: Rated 1 or 2, each with an owner
accr.trendEyebrow: Half-year self-evaluations; the last point may be a draft
accr.openBody: Opens the {cycle} self-evaluation of {p}. Training staff rate it; the training manager finalises.
accr.gapsBody: Gaps of the latest self-evaluation of each programme (draft or finalised).
accr.criteriaNote: Generic, paraphrased objectives based on the public IAEA systematic approach to training and FANR-REG-16. No accreditation-body text is reproduced.

rating.hint2: in place in part; evidence incomplete

se.mirror: Kafa'a suggests evidence from its own records; the ratings are the training staff's judgement.
se.makerChecker: Never finalised by its sole author
se.blockUnowned: Some gaps have no owner or due date
se.blockSole: You are the only person who rated it: another member of training staff must rate at least one criterion
se.suggested: Evidence Kafa'a holds for this criterion
se.noEvidenceFound: No evidence found in Kafa'a for this criterion. Rate it on evidence held elsewhere and describe it in the note.
se.finaliseBody: Readiness {pct}% with {g} gaps, each with an owner and due date. Finalising freezes the ratings and is recorded in the evidence ledger. It is a self-check, not an accreditation decision.

fx.intro: The SAT task inventory with a future layer: for each task, the OECD AI capability it needs, how far AI reaches by its change horizon, the technology that drives the change and the skills the task needs today and tomorrow.
fx.noAccess: The task layer is for training staff and auditors
fx.assumptionBody: AI capability levels are an ENEC planning assumption on the OECD five-level scale, not OECD ratings. Exposure describes what a tool could do and what people still own; it implies no staffing or deployment decision. Security, safeguards and cyber tasks are managed outside Kafa'a and never appear here.

meaning.augment: A tool can help with parts of this task; the person keeps the judgement and signs the result.
meaning.automate_partly: Parts of this task can be automated by its horizon; the person checks the output and handles the exceptions.
meaning.human_core: People own this task: AI does not reach what it needs on most dimensions.

bench.label: Benchmarks
bench.note: Benchmarks are sources Kafa'a learns from; they do not endorse this concept.

fx.tileHotSub: Driver changes at least {pct}% of tasks
fx.mixNote: Tasks, not people: no group is small enough to identify anyone.
fx.oursLabel: of {n} rated ENEC tasks are AI-assisted or partly automatable (planning assumption)
fx.oursNote: A different method from the reference study below: compare the direction, not the number.
fx.heatBody: How many tasks of each role fall in each band. Counts of tasks, never of people.
fx.hotCriteria: A role shows a driver badge when that driver changes at least {pct}% of its rated tasks, and only when the role has at least {min} rated tasks.
fx.ruleEyebrow: First match wins; the same rule runs in the browser and the database

rule.below_half: AI reaches the need on fewer than half of the rated dimensions: human core.
rule.critical_all: AI reaches the need on every dimension of a critical task: AI-assisted, a qualified person stays accountable.
rule.all_covered: AI reaches the need on every dimension: partly automatable, a person verifies.

fx.levelsCaption: AI capability reference (OECD five-level scale, planning assumption)
fx.levelsNote: The tenth OECD dimension, consciousness, is not a work-task requirement and is not rated. Levels are reviewed by the SAT team.
fx.explorerBody: Filter by role, exposure, horizon or driver; open a task to see its dimensions and edit them.
fx.restrictedNote: Security, safeguards and cyber tasks are managed outside Kafa'a and are never rated or listed.
fx.analystsBody: The training manager designates instructors who may rate task futures. Other instructors and auditors read.
fx.designateBody: {name} will be able to set the future attributes of SAT tasks. The designation is recorded in the evidence ledger.
fx.withdrawBody: {name} will no longer be able to set task future attributes. The withdrawal is recorded in the evidence ledger.
fx.readOnly: You can read the task layer. The training manager or a designated SAT analyst sets the ratings.
fx.satBody: How each role's tasks change with AI, digital I&C and robotics, rated on the OECD AI capability dimensions.
fx.cardEyebrow: OECD AI capability, horizon and driver
fx.notRated: This task has no future rating yet.

edit.title: Future attributes · {code}
edit.body: Choose 1 to 4 OECD dimensions the task really needs, the level a person must reach on each, the horizon and the driver of change, and link the skills. Each save writes one SAT change-log entry.
